chunks: Al-Tawhid: Al-Hamdani, from Ali, from his father, from Al-Harawi, from Ali ibn Musa Al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ninety-nine names. Whoever calls upon Allah by them is answered, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.

key_terms.دَعَا اللَّهَ: called upon Allah / supplicated to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the ninety-nine names of Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt chain in *Mujam al-Ahadith al-Mutabara*, emphasizes the divine attribute of responding to invocation (*Istijab*) through the ninety-nine names. While often linked to the famous *Sahih al-Bukhari* hadith, Shia scholarship highlights the unique spiritual efficacy of these names as keys to understanding God's will and attributes, serving as a practical means for believers to attain Paradise through remembrance (*Dhikr*).

en.ammaar-muslim: 9. [9/358] al-Tawhid: al-Hamdani from Ali from his father from al-Harawi from Ali b. Musa al-Ridha from his father from his forefathers from Ali عليهم السلام who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه واله said:
Allah Mighty and Majestic has ninety-nine names. Whoever asks Allah through them is answered. Whoever enumerates them enters paradise.
